content.text: Do you also want either fcrepo-message-consumer or fcrepo-camel installed and configured to allow messages to be interpreted by the Solr and/or Fuseki apps?
This may also be of interest:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/fedora-tech/-7PzQU3BBGA/agcsgMHK4eoJ
Added fcrepo-message-consumer and configured for both Solr and Fuseki.
Updated Fuseki configuration to use persistent storage location.
Tested on my MacBook using the normal Sparql recipes and got 3 records in Solr and a bunch of triples in Fuseki along with the actual objects in Fedora.
https://github.com/whikloj/fedora4-vm
After I fix the error mentioned in the README, I get the following error:
fedora4-vm$ vagrant up
Bringing machine 'default' up with 'virtualbox' provider...
[default] Clearing any previously set forwarded ports...
[default] Clearing any previously set network interfaces...
[default] Preparing network interfaces based on configuration...
[default] Forwarding ports...
[default] – 22 => 2222 (adapter 1)
[default] – 8080 => 8080 (adapter 1)
[default] – 3030 => 3030 (adapter 1)
[default] Running 'pre-boot' VM customizations...
[default] Booting VM...
[default] Waiting for machine to boot. This may take a few minutes...
The guest machine entered an invalid state while waiting for it
to boot. Valid states are 'starting, running'. The machine is in the
'poweroff' state. Please verify everything is configured
properly and try again.
If the provider you're using has a GUI that comes with it,
it is often helpful to open that and watch the machine, since the
GUI often has more helpful error messages than Vagrant can retrieve.
For example, if you're using VirtualBox, run `vagrant up` while the
VirtualBox GUI is open.
...probably a BIOS setting on my end.
I should just make a Vagrant version of > 1.6.0 a requirement.
Everything builds fine on my end. I'm on Ubuntu 14.04 and running Vagrant 1.6.5.
Can this run in Amazon EC2 instance, like Ubuntu?
Theoretically, that should be possible. If you are looking for a quick way to provision a server, this might not be the best solution though.
This looks good...
Please merge following PR if it works for you:
https://github.com/whikloj/fedora4-vm/pull/1
Ok, I merged your PR.
I updated the Sparql recipes wiki page including modifying some queries and results. These are common between in-memory and persistent storage from all my trials.
Lastly I updated the fedora4 VM to cache the downloaded files to make a rebuild faster,
Nicely done,
I have forked your project to its new home in fcrepo4-labs:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-vagrant
This task is to create a Vagrant setup that can be used in F4 one-day trainings, like the upcoming training in D.C.
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Training+-+DC+Area+Fedora+User+Group+Meeting%3A+31+March+-+1+April+2015
Ideally, this Vagrant setup would include:
Tomcat7
Fedora4
Solr
Fuseki
Here is a good starting point:
https://github.com/Islandora-Labs/islandora/blob/7.x-2.x/install/Vagrantfile
